top.title: James Trafford says he left Man City for his 'mental wellbeing'
top.description: James Trafford has admitted that he joined Leeds in the summer for his own “mental wellbeing” after a lack of game time at Manchester City left him feeling “horrendous” last season. Academy graduate Trafford rejoined City in the summer of 2025 following a two-year spell at Burnley, but saw his ambitions of becoming the club’s number one dashed when Gianluigi Donnarumma came through the door from Paris Saint-Germain in the same transfer window. Having started the opening three games of the Premier League season prior to Donnarumma’s deadline-day arrival, Trafford was subsequently relegated to second choice, with Pep Guardiola mostly deploying him in cup competitions. He made just one more league appearance in the 35 matches that followed, which came on the final day of the season in City’s 2-1 defeat at home to Aston Villa , when Arsenal had already sealed the title. "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling, not playing," Trafford told BBC Sport . "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny. "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing. Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous. "I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve." James Trafford struggled for minutes at Man City (Action Images via Reuters) Trafford nevertheless played a significant part in City’s silverware successes last season, starting between the sticks for both the Carabao Cup final triumph against Arsenal and FA Cup final win over Chelsea at Wembley. His performances did enough to earn a place in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup that summer, serving as back-up to Jordan Pickford, with Trafford completing his £45m switch to Leeds after the tournament. Despite his struggles during his City return, Trafford does take value from that year of his career. "Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added. "Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens. Trafford started both of City's victorious finals at Wembley last term (Getty) "In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year. "There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

top.title: Derek Carr breaks his silence on reports he is set to join the Minnesota Vikings
top.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings could be set to pull off something special before Tuesday’s trade deadline at the quarterback position. Kyler Murray has been sidelined for Monday’s game against the Buffalo Bills due to a hamstring injury. Carson Wentz is now set to take on the QB1 role under Kevin O’Connell, as speculation over the long-term cover at the position rumbles on in the background. “I’m watching the Vikings QB position, especially when they have an all-world defense that’s good enough to win a Super Bowl, where they need the QB to play well, where they need the offense to produce. Again, with everything going on, I’m watching the Vikings QB position,” Adam Schefter said on Friday. Naturally, this has stirred the pot, with fans putting two and two together and coming out with five. This was clearly the case as reports circulated on Friday evening that former Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Derek Carr was lined up to return to the NFL with the Vikings. Derek Carr speaks out on reports over return to NFL with the Minnesota Vikings Carr officially retired last year following 11 seasons in the league. A return for the 35-year-old has been mooted a number of times since his retirement, but it seems as if the former quarterback is content with his life away from the game. “Breaking news from the Homegrown Network here: Derek Carr is confirmed to have had a workout today with the Minnesota Vikings. Can you confirm?” said Carr’s friend. “I had a workout in Bakersfield, California, at the football facility. What?” Carr jokingly replied. The Vikings are going to have to look elsewhere, and the options for a cheap trade are extremely limited, given Nolan Teasley will want to add a QB capable of balancing the offense with their incredible defense. Considering the Vikings already have a solid backup in Wentz, the plan would surely be to bring in an actual starter from another team. However, that is not going to come cheap, but Teasley may view this as the Vikings’ opportunity to get to the Super Bowl with the way their defense is playing. Having seen the struggles the Seattle Seahawks have endured this season, Teasley will be all too aware that you have to strike while the iron is hot. top.title: Adam Scott reveals what players who have just left LIV Golf should be made to do now
top.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Adam Scott is a consummate professional in every sense. When numerous big-name players who were on the wrong side of 40 left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf four years ago, Scott was tipped to follow them. After Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, and Sergio Garcia all jumped ship from the PGA Tour, the spotlight was shining brightly on Adam Scott. However, Scott didn’t budge. He remained loyal to the PGA Tour and, by doing so, cemented his legacy as one of the game’s greatest golfers, but he also ensured he will end up on the right side of history. Now the Australian is adamant that those who played on LIV Golf should not be given a straightforward route back to the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour. Adam Scott demands former LIV golfers face a tough route back It was announced on Thursday that LIV Golf had officially folded as a business. LIV made some players wealthy beyond their wildest dreams, but the money they received obviously did not come without risk or consequence. Ben Parsons of Today’s Golfer asked Scott what he believes should happen now with the players who have just left LIV Golf. “ I mean, I think the fairest thing is that they all re-establish themselves in the system that they want to go to, whether that’s DP World or the PGA Tour, they left and gave up those privileges, “ the 46-year-old replied. “ So, you know, I think they should re-qualify themselves ideally. That’s how I would see it. I think that seems logical and sensible. “ Scott was then asked whether he thinks it’s a good thing that the best players in the world could soon be back playing together again. “ Hopefully that’s the case, yeah, “ the Australian replied. “ I mean, I think what we’ve seen with it all is, there’s probably enough events, and we have to find the right balance that everyone is kind of satisfied with guys being together enough, but there’s still enough interest and pathways and creating new talent and all this. “ And I think, you know, I think the last few years have shown us we all need to work towards making this, you know, a healthy sport and something that people get excited for. “

top.description: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is a fear among fans and media members about the power of “bulletin-board material.” According to the theory, if a player or coach says something negative (either real or perceived) about the upcoming team on the schedule, that quote will be printed out and posted on a bulletin board for everyone on the opposing team to see. It is a bit of an antiquated idea – has anyone actually used a bulletin board since the last millennium? – but it was probably always more about the message than the medium anyway. The real question is just how much does that actually happen across professional sports? These are highly skilled athletes making a good living and eager to keep it that way. Do they really need to be motivated by something another player may (or may not) have said in the build-up to the game? top.title: 3 overlooked Joe Burrow throws that helped Bengals defeat Titans
top.description: Seven players caught at least one pass from Joe Burrow in Sunday’s 43-36 overtime win for the Bengals over the Tennessee Titans. Samaje Perine and Jack Endries were both only targeted one time. Perine hauled in a nine-yard reception on the second play of overtime, and Endries hauled in a one-yard touchdown that gave the Bengals a 14-13 lead just before halftime. Coming into this season, there was a lot of conversation about the Bengals’ wide receiver depth behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Sunday, though, showed that depth is good heading into mid-November. Mike Gesicki has a touchdown in five straight games and six out of seven overall this season, and Dohnte Meyers has gone from a great training camp story to an integral part of the Bengals’ receiver room and special teams. Burrow has trust in a lot of receivers right now. Several players caught passes from Burrow in the fourth quarter and overtime Sunday in got-to-have-it situations. On a day where Burrow was historically good, three throws are getting overlooked, but they stand out for the growing trust he has in the Bengals deep group of pass catchers and also for how ridiculously accurate and prolific Joe Burrow is at throwing the football. 1. 10:07 4Q — 3rd&3 from the Bengals 34-yard line; Bengals trailing 28-23 Tensions were high in Paycor Stadium going into this play. The Bengals had just turned the ball over on their previous offensive possession, their fourth of the day, and Tennessee cashed in with a touchdown to take the lead. After a Chase Brown run on 2nd&4 gained just one yard, there were boo-birds coming down from the crowd. Then on 3rd&3, Burrow coolly found Mike Gesicki on the right side of the field for 18 yards and a badly needed first down. It was just Gesicki’s second catch of the game, but it would be the first of three receptions for him in the fourth quarter that accumulated 48 yards. Four plays after his third-down reception, Gesicki hauled in a 25-yard touchdown for his sixth score of the season and to give the Bengals a 29-28 lead. Gesicki is now tied for the most touchdowns he’s ever scored in a season, and that was back in 2020, when he caught six touchdowns in his third season with the Dolphins. This season, Gesicki has 17 receptions for 241 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 14.2 yards per reception. top.title: Heat Must Stop Making Excuses And Start Playing Hard
top.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are in trouble, and the players are finally admitting the hard truth. After a 138-117 loss to the Lakers on Monday and a loss to the Warriors on Thursday, the team sits at a disappointing 3-6 record. Opponents are scoring 123.9 points per game against them, which is the fourth-worst mark in the entire NBA. The defense has completely fallen apart, allowing teams to shoot 48.8% from the floor. That number is the third-worst in the league. It is time to stop pretending this is just a rough start and call it what it is: a failure to compete. Giannis Calls Out the Effort Problem Giannis Antetokounmpo did not sugarcoat the situation after the loss. He scored 30 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, but he knows the team effort is missing. “We’re not playing hard enough,” Antetokounmpo said, according to Field Level Media . He went on to explain that the squad lacks trust and needs to hold each other accountable on defense. Klay Thompson added 19 points and Bam Adebayo chipped in 16, but those individual numbers do not matter if the unit cannot stop the other team from scoring at will. The Heat have lost five of their first seven games, and the pattern is clear. Fatigue Is No Excuse for Bad Habits Bam Adebayo pointed to tired legs as a major cause of the breakdown. He noted that communication stops when players get worn down, leading to costly errors. “A lot of times I feel like when fatigue sets in, we stop communicating, and that’s when mistakes happen,” Adebayo said. He warned that these lapses allow bad habits to take root. The team needs to figure it out before the season slips away completely. Miami will try to reset on Wednesday night against the struggling Los Angeles Clippers in Inglewood. The Clippers are also in a mess, sitting at 1-6 after a six-game losing streak. Brandon Ingram, the Clippers’ leading scorer, is sidelined by a heel injury. Bradley Beal is also out with a knee issue. Despite the injuries, the Clippers managed to get a career-high 26 points from Kobe Sanders in their last loss. Max Strus made his debut with 11 points and offered a hopeful message about the team’s future. “Find ways to win, find ways to battle, consistently and down the stretch and we’ll get that with this group,” Strus said. He believes the squad is eager to learn and improve. Both teams are dealing with roster upheaval, but the Heat have a chance to prove they can bounce back. Giannis is listed as probable to play despite a minor wrist injury. Myron Gardner is questionable with a quad contusion. The Clippers hope to get Ingram and Yanic Konan Niederhauser back soon, but they are not there yet.

top.title: “I Carry So Much Weight on My Shoulders”: Former FSU QB Makes Emotional Admission About Mike Norvell’s Firing Nearly Three Years After Leaving
top.description: Mike Norvell. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Former FSU quarterback Jordan Travis believes he could have played a role in preventing Mike Norvell’s departure from the program. Nearly three years after his final game in Tallahassee, he admitted that he still carries guilt over the injury that changed the program’s trajectory. Norvell was fired on Sunday following Florida State’s 36-24 home loss to Clemson. The defeat dropped the Seminoles to 3-5, extending a disappointing stretch for the program. On the Nov. 6 episode of “Travis Take Two,” Travis opened up about his relationship with Norvell and explained how the coach’s firing has affected him personally. He believes his season-ending injury in 2023 ultimately changed Florida State football’s future. “It sits on me a little bit heavy. I carry so much weight on my shoulders,” Travis said. “Obviously, that 2023 season, me breaking my leg. If I don’t break my leg, Mike Norvell is still at Florida State, I believe.” Travis suffered a devastating left leg injury against North Alabama on Nov. 18, 2023, when Florida State was 10-0. Although the Seminoles won their remaining games and finished 13-0, the committee left them out of the four-team College Football Playoff. The selection committee’s decision was heavily influenced by Travis’ absence. Travis believes a playoff appearance, and potentially a national championship run, could have given the program more financial resources and national attention, ultimately keeping Norvell in Tallahassee. “If we go to the playoffs that year and go to the championship, we have a lot more money here at Florida State, and a lot more attention. Mike Norvell is still at Florida State today,” he added. Florida State’s Struggles After Jordan Travis’ Departure Norvell’s firing came after a significant decline in results. Florida State went 2-10 in 2024, followed by a 5-7 season in 2025. The Seminoles started the 2026 season 3-5, leaving the coach with a 10-22 record since Travis’ final season. Norvell’s struggles with subsequent quarterbacks, including DJ Uiagalelei, Tommy Castellanos and Ashton Daniels, contributed to the program’s disappointing run. Florida State president Richard McCullough also pointed to the team’s lack of progress when explaining the decision. “This is a big business decision. It’s the future, the fate of Florida State football. It’s the legacy that we have at Florida State and trying to get it right. That demands excellence on the field. And a trajectory going in the right direction. I’m just not seeing that trajectory,” school president Richard McCullough said at a Sunday news conference. While Travis believes his injury changed Norvell’s future, the coach’s eventual dismissal followed several seasons of struggles after the quarterback’s departure. top.title: 'Horrendous feeling!' - Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford opens up on 'losing himself' during Manchester City nightmare following Gianluigi Donnarumma transfer
top.description: Leeds United v Brentford - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford has broken his silence on a testing period at Manchester City, describing the lack of regular playing time at the Etihad Stadium as a "horrendous feeling." The England international returned to his boyhood club with high hopes, only to find himself sidelined following a high-profile transfer window move. Sidelined at the Etihad Trafford progressed through the youth ranks at Manchester City before embarking on loan spells with Accrington Stanley and Bolton Wanderers. He eventually secured a permanent switch to Burnley, where a successful two-year stint prompted the Etihad giants to bring him back last summer. The shot-stopper anticipated becoming Pep Guardiola's first-choice goalkeeper upon his return. However, those ambitions were quickly derailed when Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma arrived in Manchester on deadline day . The late signing relegated Trafford to the bench for almost the entire domestic campaign. He was completely frozen out of Premier League action from late August until Guardiola handed him a rare start against Aston Villa on the final day of the season. 'You just lose yourself' The lack of match action took a heavy mental toll on the goalkeeper. Speaking to BBC Sport , Trafford did not hold back when reflecting on his struggles. "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," Trafford admitted. "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny." That frustration ultimately drove his summer departure to Elland Road . The Leeds number one stressed that consistent minutes were essential for his health and ambitions. "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing," Trafford explained. "Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous. I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve." Two trophies in a turbulent year Despite his Premier League absence, Trafford still played a crucial role in domestic cup competitions during Guardiola's farewell season. He kept four clean sheets in six EFL Cup outings and three in six FA Cup appearances, helping City lift both trophies. "Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens," Trafford reflected on the campaign. "In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. "Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year. top.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes F1 chief Toto Wolff has defended MotoGP ’s decision to go ahead with this weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix at the Losail International Circuit, despite the difficult situation in the Middle East caused by the armed conflict pitting the United States and Israel against Iran. F1, which like MotoGP is owned by Liberty Media, is keeping a close eye on the Qatar event, which is proceeding despite strong opposition from riders in the premier class. The riders sent several letters to the organisers, MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group (MGPSEG), and held a number of meetings to express their opposition to travelling to Qatar and, ultimately, to try to prevent the race from going ahead. Neither Yamaha nor its satellite Pramac team are taking part, as the Iwata-based manufacturer prohibits its riders from travelling to areas affected by armed conflict. top.title: Ponga-inspired New Zealand reach World Cup final
top.description: Kalyn Ponga featured with a protective arm guard for New Zealand [Getty Images] New Zealand (12) 34 Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5 Tonga (10) 10 Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013. Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role. Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes. He was also involved in the Kiwis' second try of the game - as his contest with his opposite number Lehi Hopoate was crucial to Dane Gagai grounding the ball. And while the swirling wind made conditions almost unplayable at times, he repeatedly gathered high kicks and made several telling defensive contributions. One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead. The prelude to this fixture was almost every bit as gripping as the main event. Tonga's traditional war dance, the Sipi Tau, was met by New Zealand's Haka and a long stand-off between the players provided the perfect backdrop to a contest brimming with athleticism, power and superb ball-handling skills. For the second week running, Tonga fans turned out in force with the stands a sea of red. And they witnessed their side's participation in a wonderful advert for rugby league with Jojo Fifita scoring two excellent tries. However, the match ultimately swung away from them in a five-minute period after the break when New Zealand's outstanding centre Casey McLean surged over in the left corner and the wily Jahrome Hughes darted in to score. On this occasion, Kristian Woolf's team, who effectively torpedoed England's hopes of reaching the last four with a 30-12 in their opening match on 17 October, were unable to stage the same sort of fightback that helped them defeat their Pacific Island rivals Samoa last weekend. With the scoreboard, time and a gale-force wind against Tonga, Xavier Willison punished them further when they failed to gather a short drop out. And when Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad superbly grounded Erin Clark's kick, it put the gloss on a fine New Zealand performance. top.title: “Fix This ASAP Or You’re Gone”, “Give The Team Time” – Michigan Fans React as Mike Boynton Jr’s 2nd Game Ends in Defeat to UConn
top.description: Michigan assistant coach Mike Boynton Jr. practices at open practice at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Friday, April 3, 2026. Mike Boynton Jr.’s second game as the head coach of the Michigan Wolverines ended on a disappointing note. On Friday, his team lost 85-77 to the No. 4 UConn Huskies, failing to capitalize on the momentum from their 84-68 victory over the Oakland Golden Grizzlies in their season opener. After the game, fans on social media shared their thoughts about Boynton’s future with the program. “Better fix this ASAP or you’re gone,” a fan said. “We lost the best coach in college basketball and 3 lottery picks and played a natty contender game 2. Relax. That Michigan team last year was one of the best teams. EVER. Give the team time,” another fan said. Here are a few other reactions: Friday’s game was a rematch of the 2025-26 national championship showdown between these two teams. However, unlike that game, Michigan struggled to find a consistent rhythm against UConn. Trey McKenney was the top scorer for the Wolverines with 22 points, three rebounds and one assist. Roddy Gayle Jr. scored 18 points and J.P. Estrella contributed 19 points. Meanwhile, Braylon Mullins scored 23 points for UConn. Silas Demary Jr. scored 21 points and Colben Landrew scored 14 points. The Huskies improved to 2-0. Boynton joined Michigan as an assistant in 2024. He served as defensive coordinator on Dusty May’s staff. After May left to join the Dallas Mavericks in June, Boynton signed a two-year deal as his replacement in July. Mike Boynton Jr. shares his thoughts on Michigan’s loss to UConn In the postgame press conference, Mike Boynton Jr. highlighted how Friday’s game against UConn was a “great step forward.” He also said that despite winning the national championship last season, the players are relatively new to the team and need time to build chemistry. “Yeah, I’ll be honest, I think our team knows that,” Boynton said as per ‘UM Hoops’. “I just think that they’re going to keep hearing it everywhere else that they’re the defending national champions. And as I’ve said for, you know, 2 months now, like, this team isn’t defending a national championship. They’re trying to establish their own legacy. “I think today was a great step forward. …Others may disagree, but I thought our rebounding in particular was much, much improved. I thought our ability to withstand our defensive focus, even when we weren’t scoring, we maintained that a lot better. And I actually think we got better as the game went on. They were just a little bit better than we were for most of the game.” The Michigan Wolverines will next face the Marquette Golden Eagles on Nov. 11. nigeria.title: Stephanie Okechukwu: World’s tallest women’s college basketball player makes her debut
nigeria.description: It is a new era for women’s college basketball after Thursday night’s debut of 7-foot-1, 21-year-old Nigerian Stephanie Okechukwu at Texas Tech . She is world’s tallest women’s college basketball player. Texas Tech center Stephanie Okechukwu scored six points in her debut as women´s college basketball´s tallest player at 7-foot-1. The 21-year-old freshman scored her first points on a pair of free throws and added 10 rebounds and three blocks in 21 minutes in a season-opening 64-37 win over Charlotte on Thursday night, the DailyMail reports. Destinee Hooks led the Lady Raiders with 16 points. Texas Tech coach Krista Gerlich believes there´s still much room for Okechukwu to grow as a player. “She does not think she played well,” Gerlich said. “I´m excited for her and it´s only going to get better. There is definitely more.” Okechukwu is from Nigeria and eclipses the previously tallest players listed at 6-10 – Middle Tennessee State freshman Nicole Dominguez and Eastern Illinois sophomore Abbie Boutilier. Okechukwu signed with Texas Tech in January but did not play last season. After completing her high school career in Japan in 2024, she split time playing in an AAU league in the Philippines and training in Nigeria. She was initially limited to just two years of college eligibility because she took what was considered a gap year off before the NCAA granted her four years after Texas Tech filed an appeal for a waiver. nigeria.title: Lagos ranks 28th among world’s 50 most dangerous cities – Survey
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre and one of Africa’s busiest megacities, has been ranked among the world’s 50 most dangerous cities in 2026, placing 28th on a global crime index that raises fresh questions about urban safety, insecurity and the growing pressure on law enforcement. Lagos is the only Nigerian city on the ranking published by the “Numbeo Crime Index by City 2026” – a Serbia-based global data platform that compiles crowd-sourced information on crime safety, cost of living and quality of life across cities and countries. The list records Lagos with a crime index of 68.8, placing it in the high crime category under Numbeo’s classification. The index ranges from zero to 100, with scores above 60 classified as high and those above 80 as very high. Nigeria’s commercial capital is placed ahead of major cities including Damascus in Syria, New Orleans in the United States, San Juan in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic. According to the survey, five South African cities occupy positions among the top eight, with Pietermaritzburg taking the first position, followed by Pretoria in second place, Johannesburg in fifth, Durban in sixth and Port Elizabeth in eighth. Caracas, Venezuela, and Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, occupy third and fourth positions respectively. Windhoek, Namibia, comes in at number 30. The figures also point to persistent safety concerns across the Americas. Brazil has five cities among the top 25, while the United States has several, including Memphis, Detroit, Baltimore, Albuquerque and St. Louis. Other cities featured in the top 50 include Kingston in Jamaica, Mexico City, Marseille in France, Manila in the Philippines, Birmingham in the United Kingdom and Houston in the United States. Numbeo’s Crime Index draws on several indicators, among them residents’ perceptions of crime, how safe they feel walking alone during the day or at night, and their experiences or concerns about robbery, mugging, car theft, burglary, physical attacks and harassment. It also considers drug-related problems, property crime, violent crime and corruption. The ranking reflects perceptions captured by Numbeo’s survey, rather than a verified ranking of reported criminal offences. It is based on surveys completed by Numbeo website visitors and not a direct count of police-recorded offences, reported criminal incidents or official national crime statistics. Numbeo processes the responses into scores ranging from zero to 100 to make comparisons between cities possible. The organisation also acknowledges that public perceptions of crime may not always correspond with official crime figures. nigeria.title: What do Airtel, Fidelity bank and Lekki Gardens have in common?
nigeria.description: A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. One connects millions of phone calls a day. One looks after people’s money. One builds homes. It is hard to think of three Nigerian businesses with less to do with each other. Yet on Friday, 23 October, Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens found themselves on the same list. At the ARCON Special Recognition Awards (ASRA) 2026, held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria honoured a small group of advertisers for compliance. Lekki Gardens was recognised in the Real Estate and Properties category, alongside honourees that included CocaCola, Peak, Moniepoint and Chicken Republic in their own sectors. So what do they have in common? Not size, and not industry. What they share is a record. None of them entered. ARCON’s Secretariat went back through every eligible advertisement it had vetted in the period under review and picked out the advertisers with the highest volumes of approved work in each sector. A technical assessment followed, then a jury, then final ratification, with an independent audit firm checking the process from start to finish. Nobody could buy, pitch or charm their way onto that list. The only way on was to keep getting it right. There is a second thing the three share, and it is the more important one. Each of them is trusted with something people cannot afford to lose. For Airtel, it is the connection. For Fidelity Bank, it is the savings. For Lekki Gardens, it is usually both, because a home is the largest financial decision most families will ever make. That is why the company treats its adverts as promises rather than slogans. “Compliance here is not a department. It is in the DNA of the business,” says Mr Oluwole Ntia, Lekki Gardens’ Group Head of Marketing Operations, who received the award. “We do things well, do things right and protect the resources our customers entrust to us.” Founder Dr Richard Nyong has said the same thing for years, in fewer words: “If the customer does not choose you, you do not get paid.” So, what do Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens have in common? When the regulator went looking for the advertisers it could hold up as the standard, it found all three. nigeria.title: Makinde flags off 2027 presidential campaign in Bauchi, tackles APC over opposition
nigeria.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of working to undermine opposition parties and push Nigeria towards a one-party state. Makinde, who spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), described the recent Federal High Court judgment involving the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as unfortunate and a threat to democratic governance. The Oyo State governor, who was in Bauchi to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign, urged President Bola Tinubu and the APC to allow opposition parties to operate freely, insisting that Nigeria’s democracy must not be reduced to a one-party system. “There is no way Nigeria can be a one-party state; the APC must get that clear. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the APC should allow opposition to breathe,” he said. Makinde also faulted the economic policies of the Tinubu administration, arguing that major reforms were introduced without adequate planning and a clear implementation framework, thereby worsening the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. He said the country was equally battling serious insecurity, warning that the twin challenges of economic instability and insecurity required fundamental structural reforms and strong political will to overcome. The APM presidential candidate said his party’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, backed by a policy framework and manifesto, would provide an alternative approach to addressing the country’s challenges. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that respects the country’s diverse nationalities. He maintained that Nigeria’s diversity should be harnessed as a source of national strength and unity rather than allowed to fuel division. Makinde said his proposed reforms would reposition the country for sustainable economic growth, strengthen national cohesion and address the challenges undermining democratic governance. nigeria.title: Reps 2027: Isuikwuato/Umunneochi deserves tested leadership, not experiment – Onyejeocha
nigeria.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – The former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, has hit back at her detractors ahead of the 2027 polls, insisting that her track record in the House of Representatives speaks for itself and will not be dragged into petty exchanges. The four-term lawmaker and APC candidate for Isuikwuato/Umunneochi Federal Constituency made the declaration on Wednesday at her country home in Umunneochi, Abia State, where she formally inaugurated her Campaign Council. The ceremony, attended by party chieftains, political stakeholders, coordinators, and women and youth groups, saw the constitution of departments, directorates and operational units tasked with coordination, mobilisation, grassroots engagement and communication across the constituency. Taking aim at opponents she described as unprepared for the demands of representation, Onyejeocha said she would not be drawn into name calling. “My record is in the public domain. We are not here to do name-calling with amateurs who do not know what representation entails. In 2007 when I campaigned, I never insulted any of my opponents because I have always believed in issue-based politics”, she said. She maintained that real representation is proven by outcomes rather than noise, and invited the public to scrutinise her stewardship. “Representation is not about noise but about tangible results”, she said, adding that her bills, motions and constituency projects are there for verification. The lawmaker listed her legislative interventions to include bills and motions on workers’ welfare, gender equality and social justice, alongside facilitated projects such as classroom blocks, erosion control works, rural roads, solar-powered street lights and health centres across Isuikwuato and Umunneochi. She also pointed to empowerment schemes for women and youths, skills acquisition, start-up grants, agricultural inputs and job placements in federal agencies, which she said were verifiable rather than mere rhetoric. According to her, the constituency cannot afford to experiment with leadership when ranking and experience are critical in the National Assembly. “Isuikwuato/Umunneochi cannot afford to go back to political oblivion. nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. nigeria.description: Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme. Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States. He also said Iran’s forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday. “Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war,” he said. “They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence.” “Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,” he added. – Reward offered – On Friday, the US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme. In a statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.” It did not specify what type of information would warrant a $20 million reward. nigeria.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
nigeria.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. nigeria.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
nigeria.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. A critical part of thriving through a transition, a pivot or when you are starting over is to be honest about your limits. These could be the limits of your existing knowledge, expertise, and others. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: James Trafford says he left Man City for his 'mental wellbeing'
sports.description: James Trafford has admitted that he joined Leeds in the summer for his own “mental wellbeing” after a lack of game time at Manchester City left him feeling “horrendous” last season. Academy graduate Trafford rejoined City in the summer of 2025 following a two-year spell at Burnley, but saw his ambitions of becoming the club’s number one dashed when Gianluigi Donnarumma came through the door from Paris Saint-Germain in the same transfer window. Having started the opening three games of the Premier League season prior to Donnarumma’s deadline-day arrival, Trafford was subsequently relegated to second choice, with Pep Guardiola mostly deploying him in cup competitions. He made just one more league appearance in the 35 matches that followed, which came on the final day of the season in City’s 2-1 defeat at home to Aston Villa , when Arsenal had already sealed the title. "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling, not playing," Trafford told BBC Sport . "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny. "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing. Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous. "I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve." James Trafford struggled for minutes at Man City (Action Images via Reuters) Trafford nevertheless played a significant part in City’s silverware successes last season, starting between the sticks for both the Carabao Cup final triumph against Arsenal and FA Cup final win over Chelsea at Wembley. His performances did enough to earn a place in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup that summer, serving as back-up to Jordan Pickford, with Trafford completing his £45m switch to Leeds after the tournament. Despite his struggles during his City return, Trafford does take value from that year of his career. "Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added. "Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens. Trafford started both of City's victorious finals at Wembley last term (Getty) "In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year. "There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

He remained loyal to the PGA Tour and, by doing so, cemented his legacy as one of the game’s greatest golfers, but he also ensured he will end up on the right side of history. Now the Australian is adamant that those who played on LIV Golf should not be given a straightforward route back to the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour. Adam Scott demands former LIV golfers face a tough route back It was announced on Thursday that LIV Golf had officially folded as a business. LIV made some players wealthy beyond their wildest dreams, but the money they received obviously did not come without risk or consequence. Ben Parsons of Today’s Golfer asked Scott what he believes should happen now with the players who have just left LIV Golf. “ I mean, I think the fairest thing is that they all re-establish themselves in the system that they want to go to, whether that’s DP World or the PGA Tour, they left and gave up those privileges, “ the 46-year-old replied. “ So, you know, I think they should re-qualify themselves ideally. That’s how I would see it. I think that seems logical and sensible. “ Scott was then asked whether he thinks it’s a good thing that the best players in the world could soon be back playing together again. “ Hopefully that’s the case, yeah, “ the Australian replied. “ I mean, I think what we’ve seen with it all is, there’s probably enough events, and we have to find the right balance that everyone is kind of satisfied with guys being together enough, but there’s still enough interest and pathways and creating new talent and all this. “ And I think, you know, I think the last few years have shown us we all need to work towards making this, you know, a healthy sport and something that people get excited for. “

sports.title: Heat Must Stop Making Excuses And Start Playing Hard
sports.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are in trouble, and the players are finally admitting the hard truth. After a 138-117 loss to the Lakers on Monday and a loss to the Warriors on Thursday, the team sits at a disappointing 3-6 record. Opponents are scoring 123.9 points per game against them, which is the fourth-worst mark in the entire NBA. The defense has completely fallen apart, allowing teams to shoot 48.8% from the floor. That number is the third-worst in the league. It is time to stop pretending this is just a rough start and call it what it is: a failure to compete. Giannis Calls Out the Effort Problem Giannis Antetokounmpo did not sugarcoat the situation after the loss. He scored 30 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, but he knows the team effort is missing. “We’re not playing hard enough,” Antetokounmpo said, according to Field Level Media . He went on to explain that the squad lacks trust and needs to hold each other accountable on defense. Klay Thompson added 19 points and Bam Adebayo chipped in 16, but those individual numbers do not matter if the unit cannot stop the other team from scoring at will. The Heat have lost five of their first seven games, and the pattern is clear. Fatigue Is No Excuse for Bad Habits Bam Adebayo pointed to tired legs as a major cause of the breakdown. He noted that communication stops when players get worn down, leading to costly errors. “A lot of times I feel like when fatigue sets in, we stop communicating, and that’s when mistakes happen,” Adebayo said. He warned that these lapses allow bad habits to take root. The team needs to figure it out before the season slips away completely. Miami will try to reset on Wednesday night against the struggling Los Angeles Clippers in Inglewood. The Clippers are also in a mess, sitting at 1-6 after a six-game losing streak. Brandon Ingram, the Clippers’ leading scorer, is sidelined by a heel injury. Bradley Beal is also out with a knee issue. Despite the injuries, the Clippers managed to get a career-high 26 points from Kobe Sanders in their last loss. Max Strus made his debut with 11 points and offered a hopeful message about the team’s future. “Find ways to win, find ways to battle, consistently and down the stretch and we’ll get that with this group,” Strus said. He believes the squad is eager to learn and improve. Both teams are dealing with roster upheaval, but the Heat have a chance to prove they can bounce back. Giannis is listed as probable to play despite a minor wrist injury. Myron Gardner is questionable with a quad contusion. The Clippers hope to get Ingram and Yanic Konan Niederhauser back soon, but they are not there yet.

sports.title: “I Carry So Much Weight on My Shoulders”: Former FSU QB Makes Emotional Admission About Mike Norvell’s Firing Nearly Three Years After Leaving
sports.description: Mike Norvell. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Former FSU quarterback Jordan Travis believes he could have played a role in preventing Mike Norvell’s departure from the program. Nearly three years after his final game in Tallahassee, he admitted that he still carries guilt over the injury that changed the program’s trajectory. Norvell was fired on Sunday following Florida State’s 36-24 home loss to Clemson. The defeat dropped the Seminoles to 3-5, extending a disappointing stretch for the program. On the Nov. 6 episode of “Travis Take Two,” Travis opened up about his relationship with Norvell and explained how the coach’s firing has affected him personally. He believes his season-ending injury in 2023 ultimately changed Florida State football’s future. “It sits on me a little bit heavy. I carry so much weight on my shoulders,” Travis said. “Obviously, that 2023 season, me breaking my leg. If I don’t break my leg, Mike Norvell is still at Florida State, I believe.” Travis suffered a devastating left leg injury against North Alabama on Nov. 18, 2023, when Florida State was 10-0. Although the Seminoles won their remaining games and finished 13-0, the committee left them out of the four-team College Football Playoff. The selection committee’s decision was heavily influenced by Travis’ absence. Travis believes a playoff appearance, and potentially a national championship run, could have given the program more financial resources and national attention, ultimately keeping Norvell in Tallahassee. “If we go to the playoffs that year and go to the championship, we have a lot more money here at Florida State, and a lot more attention. Mike Norvell is still at Florida State today,” he added. Florida State’s Struggles After Jordan Travis’ Departure Norvell’s firing came after a significant decline in results. Florida State went 2-10 in 2024, followed by a 5-7 season in 2025. The Seminoles started the 2026 season 3-5, leaving the coach with a 10-22 record since Travis’ final season. Norvell’s struggles with subsequent quarterbacks, including DJ Uiagalelei, Tommy Castellanos and Ashton Daniels, contributed to the program’s disappointing run. Florida State president Richard McCullough also pointed to the team’s lack of progress when explaining the decision. “This is a big business decision. It’s the future, the fate of Florida State football. It’s the legacy that we have at Florida State and trying to get it right. That demands excellence on the field. And a trajectory going in the right direction. I’m just not seeing that trajectory,” school president Richard McCullough said at a Sunday news conference. While Travis believes his injury changed Norvell’s future, the coach’s eventual dismissal followed several seasons of struggles after the quarterback’s departure. sports.description: Kalyn Ponga featured with a protective arm guard for New Zealand [Getty Images] New Zealand (12) 34 Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5 Tonga (10) 10 Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013. Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role. Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes. One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead.
